shared_qualifications: C1: Nominal atomic/molar coefficients are converted only for chemistry comparison: wt.%_i = 100*n_i*M_i / sum(n_j*M_j), over the complete stated formula. CIAAW abridged standard atomic weights 2024: Al 26.982, Co 58.933, Cr 51.996, Fe 55.845, Ni 58.693, Si 28.085, B 10.81 (https://ciaaw.org/abridged-atomic-weights.htm). Calculated nominal wt.% is not a measured analysis.

C2: PDF p.2 uses saturated-KCl SCE in NaCl, but Ag/AgCl (3.5 M KCl) in HCl. Conditional 25 C comparison for HCl: E_mV(SCE)=E_mV(Ag/AgCl)+205-241=E_mV(Ag/AgCl)-36. HORIBA gives Ag/AgCl 3.5 M KCl +0.205 V vs SHE at 25 C (https://www.horiba.com/twn/water-quality/support/electrochemistry/the-basis-of-ph/electrical-potential-of-reference-electrode/); Corrtest gives saturated-KCl SCE +0.241 V vs NHE at 25 C (https://www.corrtestinstruments.com/en/02437.html). Source tests are at room temperature; reference temperature is unspecified. Thus 246 mV vs Ag/AgCl would be 210 mV vs SCE under that convention, not CRA 246 mV(SCE). Other reasonable reference constants do not justify a zero offset.

Eb is the paper's breakdown/new-pit endpoint, with transpassive behavior also discussed. PDF p.5 says general corrosion predominates for NiCoCr/NiCoCrFe and few pits are seen; retain this qualification.
